issues.failure_explanation: Lemma 2.1 asserts (2.18) unconditionally for the interior-penalty form (2.10), but the proof only yields a positive jump coefficient after choosing gamma larger than a threshold depending on mu, ||beta||_infty and the trace constants; for small gamma the symmetric interior penalty form is not coercive, so the statement as written omits a necessary hypothesis and the implied constant depends on gamma.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add 'for gamma sufficiently large (depending on mu, ||beta||_infty and shape regularity)' to Lemma 2.1 and to every downstream result relying on (2.18).
issues.overall_effect: Well-posedness of (2.23)-(2.24), (2.52)-(2.53) and all a priori estimates implicitly hold only for gamma above an unstated threshold; nothing else fails once the hypothesis is added.
issues.title: Discrete coercivity stated without the 'penalty parameter sufficiently large' hypothesis that its proof requires
issues.why_classification: A standard local hypothesis; the method, results and rates all survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $(\lambda,\mathbf{u}, p)$ and $(\lambda_{h},\mathbf{u}_{h}, p_{h})$ be the $j$th eigenpair of (\ref{s2.2})-(\ref{s2.3})

issues.failure_explanation: The identity gives (lambda_h-lambda)(u_h,v_h) exactly, and dividing requires |(u_h,u_h^*)| (or |(u_h,I_h u^*)|) to be bounded below uniformly in h. This holds only when (u,u^*) is nonzero, i.e. for non-defective eigenvalues (and h small enough that u_h->u, u_h^*->u^*). For a defective eigenvalue the eigenvector and adjoint eigenvector are orthogonal, so (u_h,v_h)->0 and (2.78) fails as stated. Lemma 2.9 imposes no such hypothesis, and Theorem 3.8 invokes it under only 'the conditions of Theorem 3.1', which also lack it.

failure_location.quote: we deduce that $|(\mathbf{u}_{h},\mathbf{v}_{h})|$ has a positive lower bound uniformly with respect to $h$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypotheses 'lambda non-defective and h sufficiently small' to Lemma 2.9 and Theorem 3.8 (the corollary already assumes non-defectiveness).
issues.overall_effect: (2.78) and hence the a posteriori eigenvalue bound (3.33) are unsupported for defective eigenvalues; the non-defective statements of Theorem 2.10 are unaffected.
issues.title: Eigenvalue error identity's uniform lower bound on |(u_h, v_h)| requires a non-defective eigenvalue, not assumed
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard hypothesis restores every claim; the paper's advertised results already target non-defective eigenvalues.

issues.failure_explanation: Bounding the right side of (2.78) with (2.15)-(2.17) and the interpolation errors of I_h u^*, vartheta_h p^* gives |lambda-lambda_h| <~ h^r(|||u-u_h||| + ||p-p_h||_0); the term A_h(u-u_h,u^*-I_h u^*) cannot be controlled by ||u-u_h||_0. The stated (2.90) with the L2 norm is not derived from the cited ingredients. With the corrected version, the equivalence (2.91) still follows, but only after an absorption argument valid for h sufficiently small, which the proof does not state.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace ||u-u_h||_0 in (2.90) by |||u-u_h||| and note that (2.91) holds for h sufficiently small via absorption of the h^r-small terms.
issues.overall_effect: The derivation of (2.91) and thus (2.81)-(2.85) rests on an incorrectly stated intermediate bound; the final rates remain correct once the argument is repaired.
issues.title: Estimate (2.90) is not what (2.78) yields: the energy norm, not the L2 norm, of u-u_h appears
issues.why_classification: A local correction of one intermediate inequality plus a standard smallness remark; all stated rates survive.

issues.failure_explanation: The last term of (3.30) equals int_F (beta.n)[[u_h]].conj(Theta) since u is continuous; bounding it gives a contribution proportional to h_F^{1/2}||[[underline u_h]]||_{0,F} (equivalently, via the trace inequality, h_F^{1/2}||u-u_h||_{0,omega(F)} plus h_F^{3/2}||grad(u-u_h)||). Neither is controlled by ||grad(u-u_h)||_{0,omega(tau)} + ||p-p_h||_{0,omega(tau)} locally, so (3.25) (and (3.28)) as stated are not established; a jump/L2 term is missing.

failure_location.quote: and by (\ref{s3.24}) and Proposition 3.37 in \cite{Verfurth2013}, we get (\ref{s3.25}).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the term (sum over faces of tau) h_F^{1/2}||[[underline u_h]]||_{0,F} (or h_tau eta_{J_tau}) to the right sides of (3.25) and (3.28).
issues.overall_effect: Only the local efficiency statements (3.25), (3.28) are affected; the global bounds of Theorem 3.6 survive because ||u-u_h||_h^2 already contains gamma h_F^{-1}||[[u_h]]||^2, which dominates the missing term.
issues.title: Local efficiency bound for the face residual omits the velocity-jump term produced by the proof
issues.why_classification: Adding a lower-order local term fixes the lemma and all global efficiency claims remain intact.

issues.failure_explanation: Inserting (3.22)-(3.23) into (2.78) yields |lambda-lambda_h| <~ (eta_h + ||lambda_h u_h - lambda u||_0 + osc)(eta_h^* + ||lambda_h^* u_h^* - lambda^* u^*||_0 + osc^*) + |lambda||(u-u_h,u^*-u_h^*)|. Theorem 3.8 states (3.33) with none of the extra terms. Since ||lambda_h u_h - lambda u||_0 >= |lambda-lambda_h| - |lambda|||u-u_h||_0, removing them requires an absorption argument using the a priori estimates (2.81),(2.83),(2.90), smallness of h and non-defectiveness; none of this is given, and 'the conditions of Theorem 3.1' do not include these hypotheses.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume lambda non-defective and h sufficiently small, retain the ||lambda_h u_h - lambda u||_0-type terms, and show via (2.81),(2.83),(2.90) that they and the L2 product term are absorbed or higher order.
issues.overall_effect: The reliability of the eigenvalue estimator (3.33) and the third inequality of the corollary are unproved as stated; they hold asymptotically for non-defective eigenvalues under the a priori theory.
issues.title: Eigenvalue reliability bound drops the ||lambda_h u_h - lambda u|| and lambda(u-u_h,u*-u_h*) terms without justification
issues.why_classification: A short standard higher-order-term argument with added hypotheses restores the stated bound; no change in method or estimator.
